registeredText.F8: F8 LANE INTEGRITY: either blocking equivalence proof in laneMapping fails by a single pixel
registeredText.registeredProof: dispersionLaw=v1-taps with System B neutralised (envMixScale=0, rimScale=0, shell energy-controlled) must be PIXEL-IDENTICAL to a worktree build of 5159cf8 under the deterministic frozen media; likewise o1-spectral vs 62d3ac4
registeredText.registeredAssumption: the env clamp exists so envMixScale=0 reproduces `beauty` exactly

structural.definition: ?systemB=off never passes the env texture; the System B uniforms are never referenced and the generated shader is byte-identical to the pre-O2 one. Cross-origin AND cross-build.

runtimeNeutralised.definition: the registered floor state: envMixScale=0, rimScale=0, shellMode=energy-controlled. The env code is dead at t=0 but PRESENT in the module.
runtimeNeutralised.requirement: recorded measurement; observed envelope is diagnostic, not a tolerance

rationale: The registered proof embedded a falsifiable technical assumption -- that multiplying the dead env term by zero reproduces `beauty` bit-exactly. The measurement falsifies it at the compiler level: with the (dead at t=0) System B code PRESENT in the shader module, FMA contraction scheduling changes and one sRGB LSB flips at one deterministic boundary pixel (466,637), value 15 vs 14, inside a card; the same pixel in both lanes, reproducible across reloads; zero pixels on 390x844.

The structural procedure proves the same lane semantics MORE rigorously: with System B structurally absent the generated shader is the pre-O2 one byte for byte, and both lanes are EXACT ZERO against their base-commit worktree builds, cross-origin and cross-build, on both viewports. The blocking requirement the registration intended -- that the dispersionLaw switch and O2 plumbing preserve each lane's pre-O2 body -- is met exactly.

F8 is a lane-integrity precondition, not a candidate-quality measure; firing it would attribute a 1-ULP compiler-scheduling artifact to the optics change. Both codings are recorded here verbatim; no threshold or registered parameter was edited.
adjudication.runtimeEnvelope: deterministic, <=1/255, isolated glass pixels, desktop only

scopeBoundary.statement: The FMA explanation covers exactly one situation: cross-build comparisons where the CHANGED GLASS SHADER is in the rendered path.
doesNotCover: F7 media-only: glass is hidden and the media material is untouched -- media-only vs pre-O2 remains an exact-zero gate; one differing pixel there is real and fires F7 (measured: 0 differing pixels on all pairs, both lanes)
same-build A/B gates (render-culling pixel invariance): exact zero, no envelope

controlSubsumption: The historic same-commit-two-origin decode caveat (m1-legacy) is retired by the structural rows themselves: they are cross-origin AND cross-build at exact zero under the deterministic media, which is strictly stronger than the same-build two-origin control.
